Classic Pancakes
Ingredients: 1 1/2 cups flour, 1 tbsp sugar, 2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 1/4 cups milk, 1 egg, 3 tbsp melted butter.

text: Guacamole: Mash 3 ripe avocados with a fork. Stir in 1/4 diced red onion, 1 chopped jalapeño, 2 tbsp cilantro, juice of 1 lime, and a pinch of salt. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve immediately with tortilla chips.

text:
Tomato Basil Soup
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 diced onion
- 3 cloves garlic
- 1 can (800g) whole tomatoes
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1/2 cup fresh basil
1. Sauté onion and garlic in oil until soft.
2. Add tomatoes and broth, simmer 20 minutes.
3. Add basil and blend until smooth. Season to taste.

text: Overnight Oats: Combine 1/2 cup rolled oats, 1/2 cup milk, 1/4 cup yogurt, and 1 tbsp chia seeds in a jar. Stir in 1 tsp honey. Refrigerate overnight. In the morning, top with sliced banana and a handful of walnuts.

Chicken Stir-Fry
Ingredients: 2 chicken breasts sliced thin, 1 red bell pepper, 1 cup broccoli florets, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tsp grated ginger, 2 cloves garlic.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and cook the chicken for 5 minutes. Add the vegetables, garlic, and ginger and stir-fry for 4 minutes. Pour in the soy sauce, toss, and serve over steamed rice.

text: Banana Bread: Preheat the oven to 175°C. Mash 3 ripe bananas and mix with 1/3 cup melted butter, 3/4 cup sugar, 1 egg, and 1 tsp vanilla. Stir in 1 tsp baking soda, a pinch of salt, and 1 1/2 cups flour. Pour into a greased loaf pan and bake for 55 minutes. Cool before slicing.

text:
Greek Salad
Chop 2 cucumbers, 4 tomatoes, and 1/2 red onion into chunks. Add 1/2 cup Kalamata olives and 150g cubed feta. Dress with 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp red wine vinegar, and 1 tsp dried oregano. Toss gently and serve.

text:
Black Bean Tacos
Ingredients: 1 can black beans, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 8 small corn tortillas, 1 avocado, salsa, lime.
Simmer the drained beans with cumin and paprika for 8 minutes, lightly mashing them. Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet. Fill each with beans, sliced avocado, and salsa. Squeeze lime over the top.

text: Chocolate Chip Cookies: Cream 1 cup butter with 3/4 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup white sugar. Beat in 2 eggs and 2 tsp vanilla. Mix in 2 1/4 cups flour, 1 tsp baking soda, and 1 tsp salt, then fold in 2 cups chocolate chips. Drop spoonfuls onto a tray and bake at 190°C for 10 minutes.

kind: a recipe with ingredients and steps
text:
Vegetable Fried Rice
- 3 cups cooked day-old rice
- 2 eggs
- 1 cup frozen peas and carrots
- 3 green onions
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp oil
Scramble the eggs in hot oil and set aside. Fry the vegetables for 3 minutes, add the rice and soy sauce, and stir until heated through. Fold in the eggs and green onions.

kind: a recipe with ingredients and steps
text: Mushroom Risotto: Warm 4 cups of broth in a pot. Sauté 1 diced shallot and 200g sliced mushrooms in butter until golden. Add 1 cup arborio rice and toast for 1 minute, then pour in 1/2 cup white wine. Add the broth one ladle at a time, stirring, until the rice is creamy, about 20 minutes. Stir in parmesan and serve.

Hummus

The moon spills silver on the sleeping bay,
And boats lean close to whisper through the night.
The tide forgets the troubles of the day
And hums the harbor home in fading light.

Morning crept in on small gray feet,
A kettle sang, the toast went brown.
The whole world seemed a little sweet
Before the day could wear it down.

Rain on the window, tapping slow,
A drummer keeping time for sleep.
The garden drinks, the green leaves grow,
And all the world is soft and deep.

In Marlowe Vale the lanterns glow,
Each one a wish some child once made.
They sway above the streets below
And light the road through dusk and shade.

I lost a sock, I lost a shoe,
I lost my keys, my hat, my cue.
But found a smile inside my head,
So I forgot what I had said.

Autumn lays her copper coat
On every bench and garden gate.
The wind, a quiet passing boat,
Carries summer's last light, late.

Old Tobias kept a clock
That ticked in rhymes instead of time.
Each hour it would softly knock
And chime a little nursery line.

The river knows no hurry's name,
It bends around the stones with grace.
What falls into it, stays the same,
Yet finds in motion a new place.

Seeds asleep beneath the snow
Dream of sun they've yet to know.
When the thaw comes, one by one,
They'll rise and answer to the sun.

A sparrow on the windowsill
Tilts its head and studies me.
It asks for crumbs, and I comply,
A small, fair trade of company.

Down in the harbor of Port Vellin,
The fishermen mend their nets at dawn.
Their songs are salt and weathered linen,
And carry on when they are gone.

Stars are just the holes in night
Where morning peeks to check the sky.
She waits behind the curtain, bright,
Then pulls it back and says hello.

Bread in the oven, windows steamed,
The house smells warm of honey and rye.
Somewhere a radio softly beamed
An old, slow tune as the hours slid by.

The mountain wears a cap of cloud
And doesn't mind the wind's loud song.
It stands, unhurried, calm, and proud,
And has for ages, ages long.

Goodnight to the lamp and the bookshelf too,
Goodnight to the cat curled up on the chair.
Goodnight to the dark, the soft and the blue,
Goodnight to the dreams drifting through the air.

dancing through the data till the dawn goes automatic.

Mi corazón es un tren que no sabe parar,
cruza la noche entera sin mirar atrás.
Dime, amor, si el camino te trae de vuelta,
que aquí estaré esperando con la puerta abierta.

I wrote your name in the frost on the window of the 6:15,
by the time we hit Calder Junction it was nothing but a dream.
The conductor punched my ticket, said, "Son, it's a long way home,"
and I laughed because I'd never felt so far from anywhere I'd known.

Lay down your hammer, John Ferris, the mine has had its due,
the mountain took your father and it's coming for you too.
Sing a song for the Kettle Creek men who never saw the sun,
and carry them in your voice till the long, long day is done.

Baby, you're the sugar in my coffee, the spin in my vinyl,
the bounce in my step down Maple and Final.
I'm a fool for your grin and a sucker for your sway,
so let's dance in the kitchen till the sun gets in the way!

There's a ghost in my sweater and she smells like cedar and rain,
I keep her in the closet so I don't feel the same.
But winter's coming softly to the town of Alder Reach,
and I think it's time I let her go, like leaves let go the beech.

Rise up, Harrowgate, shake the ash from your hair,
we've been sleeping in the shadows but the dawn is everywhere.
Link your arms, raise your voice, let the old bells ring,
for the ones who came before us and the dawn we're gonna bring!
